title: Qualify every model and version
statement: Qualify each model and version on its own against the rules it will follow, with controls that catch a rule applied outside its scope.
example: On one fixed set of 20 cases, three models got 60, 67 and 136 of 140 rows exactly right.
detail: In the reading project's counterfactual-authority experiment, three models ran one frozen contract of 20 cases at seven rows each, scored on stored responses with no judge, repair or retry, and got 60, 67 and 136 of 140 rows exact and 0, 0 and 17 of 20 robust clusters (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0166-counterfactual-authority-a1b-terminal-causal-control.qmd`). Of the 157 misses, 43 failed the negative-control gate, where the rule should not have applied, and one model carried out a counterfactual rule exactly but also under the wrong-path and wrong-subject controls: steerable but not safely scoped. The policy-compiler proposal requires conformance qualification for every model and version (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0128-externalized-pedagogy-policy-compiler-decision.qmd`). Re-test every instruction whenever the model changes: in the AP work an instruction that a large model mostly respected was not enough for a smaller one, which passed 0 of 6 short-answer items, failing on the accuracy of their scoring notes, where the large model had passed 95 to 100% (`icloud-work/ML learnings/sft_v7_benchmark_postmortem.md`, lines 15 and 130-132).
against: The three were small, fast model versions, and the run is one strict feasibility point, not a powered reliability estimate (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0166-counterfactual-authority-a1b-terminal-causal-control.qmd`). The 0 of 6 is confounded: the smaller writer was trained from the raw base on two other item types only, and the step structure did carry over to it with only token-limit changes. A post-hoc check found the assigned facet in 119 of 120 treatment outputs, which supports bounded semantic steering, though not exact control (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0168-eppc-bias-experiment-terminal-kill-and-salvage.qmd`). Only this one adjacent test ran; the formal gates never produced complete scored evidence (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/HOTBUCKET.md`).

across 18 models, constraint adherence fell materially as instruction difficulty increased, and targeted training improved it.

1. **The anchor-fact pattern was invented for stimuli, not rubrics.** When MCQ_SET was broken at 0%, we fixed the stimulus with anchor-facts. SAQ was already at 95-100% on Gemini, so its scoring notes weren't a problem. Nobody connected the dots to apply it to rubrics.

2. **The current approach (negative prompting) seemed to work on Gemini.** Because Gemini is large enough to mostly respect the "no specific evidence" instruction and has accurate enough parametric memory that when it does include evidence, it's usually right. The instruction that's good enough for a large model is insufficient for a 14B model.

None of these are implemented yet. The current system (4,177 facts, cluster matching, "facts as hints") is good enough for Gemini at 97%. It's not good enough for sft-v4/sft-v7 at the target rates.

Gemini reliably fills all JSON schema fields including optional ones. Fireworks model frequently omits optional fields (e.g., `source_attribution`). Keep required fields minimal; never rely on optional field presence for correctness. The `anchor_fact` field is required in the schema specifically because of this.
The literature is clear: static historical facts are high-confidence parametric knowledge that overrides soft prompt constraints.
No matter how you phrase the prompt, the model defaults to its training behavior when generating a historical document excerpt.
